rubric.why: Identifies what the description refers to.
rubric.how: Award for either term; both are not required for this point.

rubric.why: States that temperature expresses a degree or extent.
rubric.description: States that temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is a degree.

modelAnswer: Temperature of a body is defined as degree of its hotness or coldness.

rubric.why: Identifies temperature as a physical quantity.
rubric.description: States that temperature is a physical quantity.
rubric.how: Award for identifying temperature as a physical quantity.

rubric.why: Gives the role of temperature in determining heat-flow direction.
rubric.description: States that temperature determines the direction of flow of thermal energy.
rubric.how: Award when direction, flow and thermal energy are stated.

modelAnswer: Temperature can be defined as a physical quantity which determines the direction of flow of thermal energy.

rubric.why: Defines the property by its change with temperature.
rubric.description: States that it is a property of a substance that changes appreciably with temperature.
rubric.how: Award for linking a substance’s property changing to a change in temperature.

rubric.why: Requires at least one suitable property from the listed examples.
rubric.description: Enlists at least one suitable thermometric property or thermometer-material characteristic.
rubric.how: Award for any one listed characteristic.

modelAnswer: A thermometric property is a property of a substance that changes appreciably with temperature.

Suitable thermometer materials conduct heat well, respond quickly, expand uniformly, have a high boiling point and low freezing point, have large expansivity, do not wet glass or vapourize, and are visible.

rubric.why: Names the Celsius scale, also called the centigrade scale.
rubric.description: Names the Celsius or centigrade scale.
Names both the Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales.
rubric.how: Award only when both Fahrenheit and Kelvin are named.

modelAnswer: Three different scales are: (i) Celsius or centigrade scale (ii) Fahrenheit scale (iii) Kelvin scale

rubric.why: Captures the molecular energies that make up internal energy.
rubric.description: Defines internal energy as the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of the molecules.
rubric.how: Award when both kinetic and potential energy of the molecules are included.

rubric.why: Defines heat as energy transfer caused by a temperature difference.
rubric.description: States that heat is energy transferred from one object to another because of a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award when transfer of energy and the temperature difference are both stated.

modelAnswer: The sum of kinetic and potential energies of the molecules of an object is called its internal energy. Heat is the energy which is transferred from one object to another due to difference of temperature between the two bodies.

rubric.why: States the direct effect of heating on temperature.
rubric.description: States that the temperature rises when a substance is heated.
rubric.how: Award for stating that temperature rises or increases.

rubric.why: States the change in molecular motion and its energy consequence.
rubric.description: States that molecular motion becomes more vigorous, increasing the molecules’ kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award when increased or more vigorous molecular motion and increased kinetic energy are both given.

modelAnswer: When a substance is heated, its temperature rises and its molecular motion becomes more vigorous which increases the kinetic energy of the molecules.
